claim: Antimicrobial score grid: the printed row ('Tail total') marginal
locus_a: SI Table S3, page S10, the 'Tail total' column: 38, 40, 47, 51, 39, 51, 43, 48, 49, 42, 25, 15, 12 (sum 500)
locus_b: The same table's own 104 cells, which sum by row to 38, 40, 41, 46, 34, 45, 38, 42, 43, 35, 19, 12, 6 (sum 439)
what_we_emitted: THE CELLS. 05_values.csv carries the 104 individual scores; no row or column total is emitted.
why: 11 of 13 printed row totals exceed the cells they total, by 3 to 7 (only tails 6B and 8 reconcile). The cells are independently corroborated: 7 of 8 printed COLUMN totals reconcile with them exactly, and every one of the 27 cells covered by main-text Table 1 satisfies the identity score==6 <-> MIC<=25 uM (07_qc.json P7, 27/27). Both reads of the cells agree -- pdfplumber word coordinates and a 600 dpi render read by eye, 104/104. One residual is 7, which no single missing score 0-6 could produce, so this is not a dropped ninth column.

locus_b: Figure 1A, which draws 3NB as tris(2-aminoethyl)amine (4 N, 146.23 Da -> 0.027353) and 4NC as cyclam (4 N, 200.32 Da -> 0.019967)
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Descriptors are not emitted. 01_blocks.csv records both the computed and the printed value and flags the two that disagree.
why: Each printed value is the OTHER structure's computed value to four decimal places (07_qc.json P4, each_mismatch_is_the_others_value = true), so the two entries are transposed rather than wrong. Three further things point the same way and none of them is this arithmetic: (a) 6 of 8 rows are exact under the same definition; (b) the paper's own stated trend is that LOWER charge density scores higher, and with the printed values Spearman(charge density, head total) = +0.259, the wrong sign, while with the computed values it is -0.247, the stated sign (07_qc.json P11); (c) our 4NC parent structures match data/data_vitro.csv's KW_2014 'A138_C10' and 'A138_C12' by FULL InChIKey, independently confirming the cyclam reading. A fourth line was found afterwards and is the most direct: SI Figure S1 panel (E) draws 4NC9 in full with its headgroup protons labelled, and the labels state the ring spacers -- d, b', d (three carbons) between one pair of nitrogens and d, d (two carbons) between the next, alternating. That is cyclam; cyclen would be 2,2,2,2. The 4NC9 C10 anchor is built from that panel and matches the enumeration by full InChIKey (07_qc.json P13).

claim: 'the 20 lipidoids from this smaller library that showed antibacterial activity at 25 uM in the initial screen'
locus_b: SI Table S3 (21 of the 27 selected members carry score 6, i.e. activity at 25 uM) AND main-text Table 1 (21 of the 27 have MIC <= 25 uM) -- two independently produced tables agreeing with each other
what_we_emitted: Nothing is emitted for this sentence. 05_values.csv carries the per-member scores and MICs from which either count can be recomputed.
why: The two tables agree on 21 and on WHICH 21 (07_qc.json P7 and P10). A prose count is the weakest of the three loci, so the discrepancy is recorded against the prose rather than treated as evidence against either table.

claim: Therapeutic index of 4NC8 printed without a bound
locus_b: Main-text Table 1: 4NC8 MIC = 100 uM, and the eight BOUNDED entries in Table 2 are all exactly 400/MIC -- so TI 4 at MIC 100 implies HC50 = 400 uM, which is the authors' encoding of the '>200 uM' hemolysis category
what_we_emitted: 05_values.csv records HC50 for 4NC8 as the arithmetic product 400.0, not as '>200'.
why: Every other entry implying HC50 above the 200 uM ceiling carries '>='; this one does not, so either the sign was dropped or 4NC8's hemolysis genuinely reached 50% at 400 uM, which the stated assay range (up to 200 uM) does not cover. 07_qc.json P8 records that all 8 bounded entries hit 400/MIC exactly, which is what makes the omission visible.

claim: 'Methylation of lipidoid secondary amines affords ammonium groups'
locus_b: Figure 1A's product panel, which methylates four TERTIARY nitrogens -- including the central nitrogen of tris(2-aminoethyl)amine, which never reacted with an acrylate and was tertiary from the start; after exhaustive Michael addition no secondary amine remains anywhere in the library
what_we_emitted: The fully methylated cation, with one methyl and one positive charge on EVERY nitrogen, per the drawing. 03_enumerated.csv asserts this ledger per member and refuses a nitrogen that is not already fully substituted.
why: The prose names the wrong amine class. The figure is the specific statement and the prose is the loose one, so the figure is followed. Noted because it is the only sentence bearing on the degree of quaternisation, and the paper reports no analysis (no NMR integral, no elemental analysis, no titration) that quantifies it -- so completeness of methylation rests on the drawing alone. See DECISIONS.md D-2.

claim: Size and cross-reference of the 2 uM DLS aggregates
locus_a: Main text, Correlating Antimicrobial Activity with Lipidoid Self-Assembly: 'aggregates of 100-1000 um in size at concentrations of 2 uM (Figure S1)'
locus_b: Main text, Modular Synthesis: 'aggregates in the range of 100-1000 nm in LB medium (Figure S2)'; and SI Figure S1 is the 1H NMR panel while SI Figure S2 is the DLS data at 2 uM
what_we_emitted: Nothing -- particle size is not a value this curation emits.
why: Two errors in one clause: the unit (um for nm, a factor of 1000, and 1 mm aggregates in a broth culture are not physical) and the figure number (S1 is NMR, S2 is the DLS). Recorded because an automated size-extractor would take the number at face value.

claim: Lower lipidoid concentration in the propidium iodide assays
locus_a: Main text and Figure 3 caption: '6 uM (blue triangles)'
locus_b: SI Figure S8, S9 and S10 captions, all three: '6.25 uM (blue)'
what_we_emitted: Nothing -- PI fluorescence is not a value this curation emits. 05_values.csv's dose field records the screen and MIC doses only.
why: 6.25 uM is a two-fold dilution of 12.5 and sits on the paper's own dilution ladder, so the main text's '6' is most likely a rounding; but three SI captions say one thing and the main text plus its own figure caption say another, and neither locus is more primary than the other for this quantity.

claim: SI Figure S1 panel (A) draws the 3N headgroup as a RING
locus_a: SI Figure S1 panel (A), page S3: the blue core of '3N6B (v)' is three nitrogens each joined to the other two by a two-carbon bridge -- a 9-membered 1,4,7-triazacyclononane -- while carrying FIVE acrylate arms
locus_b: Figure 1A's 'Linear' box, which draws 3N as H2N-CH2CH2-NH-CH2CH2-NH2 (diethylenetriamine); SI Table S5's charge density for 3N of 0.0291; and the article's statement that 3N gives 5 tails
what_we_emitted: Diethylenetriamine, per Figure 1A. 03_enumerated.csv builds all thirteen 3N members on the linear triamine.
why: The panel is self-contradictory before any outside evidence: every nitrogen in a triazacyclononane has exactly one N-H, so that core can carry at most THREE arms, and the panel draws five (07_qc.json P15). Outside evidence agrees: 3/103.17 (linear) = 0.029079 matches the printed 0.0291 while 3/129.21 (ring) = 0.023219 does not, and our linear 3N14 and 3N16 parents match data/data_vitro.csv's KW_2014 'A114_C10'/'A114_C12' and NC_2024 'A113_O10'/'A113_O12' by FULL InChIKey. Figure S1 is an NMR peak-assignment cartoon on a page with no text layer; the error is in the cartoon. Recorded because connectivity is exactly what formula and mass cannot see, and a reader taking the SI drawing at face value would enumerate thirteen wrong structures.
